newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurds of KDP take last rival PUK stronghold.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds of KDP take last rival PUK stronghold.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish militia backed by Baghdad said it had entered its longtime rival faction's last stronghold on Monday to take charge in northern Iraq.

Residents of Sulaimaniya greeted fighters of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) with flowers as they entered the city, the biggest of Iraqi Kurdistan with a population of a million, said KDP politburo member Dr Ross Nouri Shawis.
There was no immediate comment from the rival group, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).

In Dukan, a town about 70 km (45 miles) away which the KDP seized from the PUK earlier in the day, Shawis told reporters: "KDP troops entered Sulaimaniya from the direction of Halabja at 7 p.m. (1500 GMT). They were welcomed by the local population with flowers."

He said the only "serious resistance" along a 76-km (46-mile) route from Halabja near the Iranian border, east of Sulaimaniya, was at Sayed Sadeq, a major highway junction at the 50-km (30-mile) mark.

Shawis received word in a military dispatch delivered by hand. Earlier in the day KDP commander Massoud Barzani, leading his forces from Dukan north of Sulaimaniya, said he did not expect to move on the city on Monday.
